1.1.t: Dhritarashtra said: Assembled on the holy field of Kurukshetra, eager for battle, what did my sons and the sons of Pandu do, O Sanjaya?

1.2.t: Sanjaya said: Then, seeing the army of the Pandavas arrayed in battle formation, King Duryodhana approached his teacher and spoke these words.

1.3.t: Behold, O teacher, this great army of the sons of Pandu, arrayed in battle formation by the son of Drupada, your intelligent disciple.

1.4.t: Here are mighty warriors and great bowmen, equal in battle to Bhima and Arjuna — Yuyudhana, Virata, and Drupada, the great chariot-warrior.

1.5.t: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi, Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best among men.

1.6.t: The valiant Yudhamanyu and the mighty Uttamaujas, the son of Subhadra and the sons of Draupadi — all of them indeed great chariot-warriors.

1.7.t: But know also, O best among the twice-born, those who are distinguished among us, the leaders of my army; I name them to you for your information.

1.10.t: Our army, marshalled under the protection of Bhishma, is unlimited, while this army of theirs, marshalled under the protection of Bhima, is limited.

1.11.t: Therefore, all of you, stationed in your respective positions at every strategic point, must protect Bhishma alone, each and every one of you.

1.18.t: Drupada and the sons of Draupadi, all of them, O ruler of the earth, and the mighty-armed son of Subhadra, blew their conch shells each separately.

1.20.t: Then, seeing the sons of Dhritarashtra arrayed in battle formation, as the clash of weapons was about to begin, the son of Pandu, whose banner bore a monkey, took up his bow and spoke these words to Hrishikesha, O King.

1.21.t:
Arjuna said: O Achyuta, place my chariot in the middle between the two armies, O lord of earth.

Wait — let me reconsider the structure. "Mahīpate" is Sanjaya addressing Dhritarashtra, and "Achyuta" is Arjuna addressing Krishna. Let me re-translate:

Sanjaya said: Arjuna then spoke these words to Hrishikesha, O lord of earth: O Achyuta, place my chariot between the two armies.

1.22.t: So that I may look upon these warriors arrayed here eager to fight, and know with whom I must do battle in this great combat.

1.23.t: I wish to observe those who have assembled here, ready to fight, desiring to please the evil-minded son of Dhritarashtra in battle.

1.25.t: In the presence of Bhishma, Drona, and all the rulers of the earth, he said, "O Partha, behold these Kurus assembled together.

1.26.t: There Partha saw stationed fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, and friends as well.

1.31.t: I see only adverse omens, O Keshava, and I do not foresee any good from killing my own kinsmen in battle.

1.33.t: Those for whose sake we desire kingdom, enjoyments, and pleasures — they stand here arrayed in battle, having given up their lives and wealth.

1.37.t: Therefore, it is not right for us to kill the sons of Dhritarashtra, our own kinsmen; for how can we be happy after slaying our own people, O Madhava?

1.41.t: O Krishna, when irreligion prevails, the women of the family become corrupt; and when women are corrupted, O Varshneya, there arises an intermixture of castes.

1.42.t: Such intermixture of castes leads to hell both the destroyers of the family and the family itself; for their ancestors fall, deprived of the offerings of rice-balls and water.

1.43.t: By these sins of the destroyers of the family, which cause the intermixture of castes, the eternal duties of the community and the traditions of the family are ruined.

1.44.t: O Janardana, we have heard that for those human beings whose family traditions have been destroyed, dwelling in hell for an indefinite period is certain.

1.45.t: Alas, what a great sin we have resolved to commit, that out of greed for the pleasures of a kingdom we are prepared to slay our own kinsmen!

2.2.t: The Blessed Lord said: Whence has this delusion come upon you at this hour of peril, O Arjuna — this which is practiced by the ignoble, which does not lead to heaven, and which brings disgrace?

2.5.t: Indeed, it is better to live even by begging in this world than to slay these noble-souled teachers. But if I were to kill these teachers, who desire wealth and gain, I would only enjoy pleasures here that are tainted with blood.

2.6.t: We do not know which would be better for us — whether we should conquer them or they should conquer us. The very sons of Dhritarashtra, after slaying whom we would not wish to live, stand arrayed before us.

2.7.t: My nature afflicted by the flaw of faint-heartedness, my mind confused about duty, I ask You — tell me decisively what is best for me. I am Your disciple; instruct me, who have taken refuge in You.

2.8.t: I do not see what could drive away this grief that dries up my senses, even if I were to attain on earth an unrivalled and prosperous kingdom, or even sovereignty over the gods.

2.9.t: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Gudakesha, the scorcher of foes, said to Govinda, "I shall not fight," and fell silent.

2.14.t: O son of Kunti, the contacts of the senses with their objects give rise to cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and are impermanent; endure them, O Bharata.

2.15.t: O noblest among men, the steady person whom these do not torment, who remains equal in pain and pleasure — he becomes fit for immortality.

2.16.t: The unreal has no existence, and the real never ceases to be; the conclusion regarding both of these has been seen by the seers of Truth.

2.24.t: This soul cannot be cut, cannot be burnt, cannot be wetted, and cannot be dried. It is eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable, and primordial.

2.28.t: Beings are unmanifest in their beginning, manifest in their middle state, and unmanifest again in their end, O Bharata — what cause is there then for lamentation?

2.29.t: Someone sees this soul as a wonder, another likewise speaks of it as a wonder, and yet another hears of it as a wonder — and even after hearing of it, no one truly understands it.

2.30.t: The embodied Self in everyone's body is always indestructible, O Bharata; therefore, you should not grieve for any living beings.

2.31.t: Moreover, considering your own duty as well, you should not waver, for there exists nothing better for a Kshatriya than a righteous war.

2.32.t: O Partha, happy are the Kshatriyas who obtain such a battle, which comes unsought and stands as an open door to heaven.

2.33.t: But if you do not fight this righteous war, then, abandoning your own duty and fame, you will incur sin.

2.36.t: Your enemies will speak many unspeakable words, denigrating your might. What could be more painful than that?

2.38.t: Treating happiness and sorrow, gain and loss, victory and defeat alike, then engage in battle; thus you shall not incur sin.

2.41.t: O joy of the Kurus, on this path the resolute intellect is single-pointed; but the thoughts of the irresolute are many-branched and endless.

2.43.t: Full of desires, with heaven as their highest goal, their words promise rebirth as the fruit of actions, abound in elaborate rituals, and are directed toward the attainment of enjoyment and power.

2.44.t: For those deeply attached to enjoyment and power, whose minds are carried away by that flowery speech, the resolute intellect directed toward samadhi is never established.

2.46.t: Whatever purpose a small well serves when water floods everywhere on all sides, that much alone is the purpose of all the Vedas for a Brahmana who truly knows.

2.48.t: Steadfast in Yoga, perform your actions, O Dhananjaya, abandoning attachment and remaining equal in success and failure; such equanimity is called Yoga.

2.50.t: One who is endowed with wisdom casts off here both good and evil deeds; therefore, devote yourself to yoga — yoga is skill in action.

2.53.t: When your intellect, which has been confused by the diverse teachings of the scriptures, stands firm and unwavering, steady in deep absorption, then you will attain Yoga.

2.55.t: The Blessed Lord said: When one completely abandons all desires dwelling in the mind, O Partha, and is satisfied in the Self by the Self alone, then one is said to be of steady wisdom.

2.56.t: He whose mind is unperturbed in sorrows, who has no craving for pleasures, and who is free from attachment, fear, and anger — he is called a sage of steady wisdom.

2.57.t: He who is without attachment to anything anywhere, who neither rejoices nor recoils upon encountering good or evil — his wisdom is firmly established.

2.58.t: When one completely withdraws the senses from the objects of the senses, as a tortoise withdraws its limbs into its shell, his wisdom is firmly established.

2.61.t: Restraining all of them, one should sit steadfast in yoga, devoted to Me as the supreme; for the wisdom of one whose senses are under control is firmly established.

2.64.t: But one who moves among sense objects with senses that are free from attachment and aversion, with those senses under one's own control, such a self-disciplined person attains serenity.

2.65.t: In that serenity, the destruction of all sorrows arises; for the intellect of one whose mind is serene soon becomes firmly established.

2.68.t: Therefore, O mighty-armed one, he whose senses are completely restrained from their sense objects on all sides — his wisdom is firmly established.

2.69.t: That which is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake; that in which all beings are awake, that is night for the seeing sage.

2.72.t: This is the state of being established in Brahman, O Partha. Having attained this, one is never deluded. Being established in this state, even at the hour of death, one attains liberation in Brahman.

3.4.t: Not by abstaining from actions does a person attain freedom from action, nor by renunciation alone does he achieve perfection.

3.6.t: He who, restraining the organs of action, sits dwelling in the mind on the objects of the senses, that deluded soul is called a hypocrite.

3.7.t: But one who, controlling the senses by the mind, engages in Karma Yoga with the organs of action, without attachment, O Arjuna — that person excels.

3.10.t: Having created beings together with sacrifice in the beginning, Prajapati said: "By this shall you prosper; let this be the wish-fulfilling cow that grants your desires.

3.12.t: Nourished by sacrifice, the gods will surely bestow upon you the desired enjoyments. He who enjoys what is given by them without offering anything back to them is verily a thief.

3.14.t: From food all beings come into existence; from rain food is produced; from sacrifice rain comes forth; and sacrifice is born of action.

3.15.t: Know that action originates from the Vedas, and the Vedas arise from the Imperishable. Therefore, the all-pervading Brahman is eternally established in sacrifice.

3.17.t: But the person who delights only in the Self, who is satisfied with the Self, and who is content in the Self alone — for him there is no duty to be done.

3.23.t: For if I were not to engage tirelessly in action at any time, O Partha, men would follow My path in every way.

3.26.t: A wise person should not unsettle the minds of the ignorant who are attached to action; rather, remaining steadfast and properly performing all actions himself, he should encourage them to do the same.

3.29.t: Those who are deluded by the gunas of Prakriti become attached to the actions of the gunas. The one who knows the whole should not unsettle those dull-witted ones of incomplete knowledge.

3.34.t: Attachment and aversion are situated in each sense toward its respective object; one should not come under the sway of these two, for they are surely one's adversaries.

3.37.t: The Blessed Lord said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of rajas, all-devouring and greatly sinful — know this to be the enemy here in this world.

3.39.t: O son of Kunti, knowledge is enveloped by this perpetual enemy of the wise, which takes the form of desire and is insatiable like fire.

3.40.t: The senses, the mind, and the intellect are said to be its seat; through these, it veils knowledge and deludes the embodied soul.

3.43.t: Thus, knowing that which is superior to the intellect, and steadying the lower self by the higher Self, O mighty-armed one, slay this formidable enemy in the form of desire.

4.2.t: Thus received through an unbroken succession, the royal sages knew this yoga. But over a great passage of time, this yoga has been lost in this world, O Parantapa.

4.4.t: Arjuna said: Your birth was later, while the birth of Vivasvan was earlier. How am I to understand that You taught this in the beginning?

4.5.t: The Blessed Lord said: Many births of Mine have passed, and of yours as well, O Arjuna. I know them all, but you do not know them, O scorcher of foes.

4.6.t: Though I am unborn, though my nature is imperishable, and though I am the Lord of all beings, I manifest Myself by My own Maya, presiding over My own Prakriti.

4.7.t: Whenever there is a decline of righteousness and a rise of unrighteousness, O Bharata, then I manifest Myself.

4.8.t: For the protection of the righteous, for the destruction of the wicked, and for the reestablishment of dharma, I manifest age after age.

4.10.t: Freed from attachment, fear, and anger, wholly absorbed in Me, taking refuge in Me, and purified by the austerity of knowledge, many have attained My state of being.

4.11.t: In whatever way people approach Me, in that very same way do I reciprocate with them; it is My path that all human beings follow in every way, O Partha.

4.12.t: Desiring success in their actions, they worship the gods in this world; for in the human world, success born of action comes quickly.

4.13.t: The four categories of society were created by Me according to the division of qualities and actions. Though I am the creator of this system, know Me to be the non-doer and the immutable.

4.18.t: He who sees inaction in action and action in inaction — he is the wise one among men; he is a yogi and the performer of all actions.

4.24.t: The ladle is Brahman, the oblation is Brahman, offered by Brahman into the fire of Brahman; Brahman alone is to be reached by one who is absorbed in seeing Brahman in every action.

4.25.t: Some yogis devote themselves to sacrifice directed to the gods alone, while others offer sacrifice by sacrifice itself into the fire of Brahman.

4.27.t: Others offer all the functions of the senses and the functions of the life breath into the fire of the yoga of self-restraint, kindled by knowledge.

4.28.t: Some offer material possessions as sacrifice, some offer austerity as sacrifice, and some offer yoga as sacrifice; while others, ascetics of strict vows, offer the study of scriptures and knowledge as sacrifice.

4.29.t: Others offer the outgoing breath into the incoming breath, and the incoming breath into the outgoing breath, while still others, restraining the movements of both the outgoing and incoming breaths, are wholly devoted to the control of breath. Yet others, having regulated their diet, offer the life-breaths into the life-energy — all these are knowers of sacrifice, whose impurities are destroyed by sacrifice.

4.30.t: Others, having regulated their food, offer the life-breaths into the life-breaths. All these are knowers of sacrifice, whose sins have been destroyed by sacrifice.

4.31.t: Those who partake of the nectarean remnants of sacrifice attain the eternal Brahman. Even this world is not for one who performs no sacrifice — how then the other, O best of the Kurus?

4.32.t: Thus, many kinds of sacrifices are spread forth at the mouth of Brahman. Know them all to be born of action; knowing thus, you shall be liberated.

4.35.t: Knowing which, O Pandava, you shall never again fall into such delusion, and by which you shall see all beings without exception in the Self and also in Me.

4.37.t: Just as a blazing fire reduces firewood to ashes, O Arjuna, so does the fire of knowledge reduce all actions to ashes.

4.42.t: Therefore, cutting asunder with the sword of knowledge this doubt of the self, born of ignorance and dwelling in the heart, take refuge in Yoga and arise, O Bharata.

5.4.t: It is the ignorant, not the wise, who speak of Sankhya and Yoga as distinct; one who is properly established in even one of them obtains the fruit of both.

5.6.t: But renunciation, O mighty-armed one, is difficult to attain without Yoga; the sage who is equipped with Yoga reaches Brahman without delay.

5.11.t: Yogis, having abandoned attachment, perform actions merely with the body, mind, intellect, and even with the senses alone, for the purification of the self.

5.12.t: The disciplined one, having renounced the fruit of action, attains everlasting peace; the undisciplined one, impelled by desire and attached to the fruit, becomes bound.

5.18.t: The wise see with equal vision a Brahmin endowed with learning and humility, a cow, an elephant, a dog, and even a dog-eater.

5.19.t: Even here in this world, creation is conquered by those whose minds are established in equanimity; for Brahman is flawless and equal, and therefore they are seated in Brahman.

5.23.t: He who is able here itself, before liberation from the body, to withstand the impulse born of desire and anger — that person is a yogi, that person is a happy man.

6.1.t: The Blessed Lord said: He who performs his obligatory duty without depending on the fruit of action — he is a sannyasi and a yogi, not one who is merely without fire nor one who is without action.

6.2.t: What they call renunciation, know that to be yoga, O Pandava; for no one who has not given up selfish resolve ever becomes a yogi.

6.3.t: For the sage who wishes to ascend to Yoga, action is said to be the means; for that same sage who has ascended to Yoga, tranquility alone is said to be the means.

6.4.t: When one is not attached to sense objects nor to actions, having renounced all desires and intentions, then one is said to have ascended to Yoga.

6.5.t: One should uplift oneself by oneself and not let oneself sink down, for the self alone is the friend of the self, and the self alone is the enemy of the self.

6.6.t: For one who has conquered the self by the self, the self is a friend of the self; but for one whose self is unconquered, the self remains in enmity, acting like an enemy.

6.8.t: The yogi whose self is satisfied with knowledge and realized wisdom, who stands unmoved, who has conquered the senses, and to whom a clod of earth, a stone, and gold are the same, is said to be a yukta — one who is united in yoga.

6.11.t: In a clean place, having established a firm seat for himself, neither too high nor too low, covered with kusha grass, then a deerskin, and a cloth one over the other—

6.12.t: Seated there on that seat, making the mind one-pointed and controlling the activities of the mind and senses, he should practice yoga for the purification of the self.

6.14.t: Serene in mind, free from fear, established in the vow of celibacy, controlling the mind and fixing it on Me, one should sit absorbed in yoga, having Me as the supreme goal.

6.15.t: Thus, ever disciplining the mind in this way, the yogi of controlled mind attains the peace that culminates in supreme liberation and that abides in Me.

6.18.t: When the fully controlled mind rests in the Self alone, free from craving for all objects of desire, then one is said to be united in Yoga.

6.19.t: As a lamp in a windless place does not flicker — such is the simile used for the yogi of controlled mind who is engaged in the practice of yoga of the Self.

6.20.t: Where the mind, restrained by the practice of Yoga, attains quietude, and where, seeing the Self by the self, one is satisfied in the Self alone—

6.28.t: Thus always engaging the mind in yoga, the yogi, freed from sin, easily attains the supreme bliss of contact with Brahman.

6.32.t: O Arjuna, he who, by comparison with himself, sees equally everywhere, whether in happiness or in sorrow, that yogi is considered the highest.

6.36.t: Yoga is difficult to attain by one whose mind is uncontrolled — this is my conviction; but by one whose mind is subdued and who strives through proper means, it is possible to attain.

6.37.t: Arjuna said: One who possesses faith but lacks sufficient effort, whose mind strays from Yoga, and who fails to attain perfection in Yoga — what destination does he reach, O Krishna?

6.44.t: By that very former practice, he is carried forward even helplessly; and even one who merely wishes to know about Yoga transcends the word-Brahman.

6.46.t: The yogi is superior to the ascetics, and is considered superior even to the men of knowledge; the yogi is also superior to the men of ritual action. Therefore, O Arjuna, become a yogi.

7.1.t: The Blessed Lord said: O Partha, with your mind attached to Me, practicing yoga and taking refuge in Me, hear how you shall know Me completely and without doubt.

7.2.t: I shall declare to you in full this knowledge along with realization, having known which nothing else remains here to be known.

7.3.t: Among thousands of men, scarcely one strives for perfection; and even among those who strive and have attained perfection, scarcely one knows Me in truth.

7.6.t: Know that all beings have these two natures as their source. I am the origin and likewise the dissolution of the entire universe.

7.11.t: I am the strength of the strong, devoid of desire and passion, and I am the desire in all beings that is not opposed to dharma, O best of the Bharatas.

7.16.t: Four kinds of virtuous people worship Me, O Arjuna: the distressed, the seeker of knowledge, the seeker of wealth, and the man of wisdom, O best of the Bharatas.

7.19.t: At the end of many births, the one endowed with knowledge surrenders unto Me, realizing that Vasudeva is all — such a great soul is exceedingly rare.

7.21.t: Whatever form a devotee wishes to worship with faith, I make that very faith of his firm and unwavering.

7.22.t: Endowed with that faith, he engages in the worship of that deity and obtains from it his desires, which are indeed granted by Me alone.

7.24.t: The unintelligent regard Me, the unmanifest, as having come into manifestation, not knowing My supreme nature, which is imperishable and unsurpassable.

7.25.t: Veiled by Yoga-Maya, I am not manifest to all. This deluded world does not know Me, the unborn and imperishable.

7.26.t: I know the beings of the past, the present, and the future, O Arjuna, but no one knows Me.

7.27.t: O Bharata, O conqueror of foes, through the delusion of duality arising from desire and aversion, all beings fall into bewilderment at the time of their birth.

7.30.t: Those who know Me together with the Adhibhuta, the Adhidaiva, and the Adhiyajna — they, with minds united in Me, know Me even at the time of death.

8.2.t: Who is Adhiyajna, and how does he exist here in this body, O Madhusudana? And how, at the time of death, are You to be known by those of steadfast mind?

8.3.t: The Blessed Lord said: The imperishable is the supreme Brahman; one's own nature is called Adhyatma; the creative offering that brings about the existence and manifestation of beings is known as Karma.

8.4.t: Adhibhuta is the perishable nature of being, and the Purusha is the Adhidaivata. The Adhiyajna is I Myself, here in this body, O best among the embodied.

8.5.t: And whoever, at the time of death, departs leaving the body while remembering Me alone, he attains My state — there is no doubt about this.

8.6.t: Whatever being one remembers while giving up the body at the end, that very being one attains, O son of Kunti, having always been absorbed in thought of that being.

8.8.t: O Partha, with a mind engaged in the yoga of practice and not straying to anything else, one who constantly meditates attains the Supreme Divine Person.

8.15.t: Having attained Me, the great souls who have reached the highest perfection do not undergo rebirth, which is the abode of sorrow and is impermanent.

8.18.t: At the coming of day, all manifested beings emerge from the Unmanifest; at the coming of night, they dissolve back into that very same which is called the Unmanifest.

8.19.t: O Partha, this same multitude of beings, coming into existence again and again, is helplessly dissolved at the coming of night and comes forth at the coming of day.

8.22.t: That Supreme Person, O Partha, within whom all beings reside and by whom all this is pervaded, is attainable indeed through unswerving devotion.

8.25.t: Smoke, night, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the sun's southern course—passing along that path and attaining the lunar light, the yogi returns.

9.1.t: The Blessed Lord said: To you who are free from envy, I shall declare this most secret knowledge combined with realized knowledge, knowing which you shall be released from all that is inauspicious.

9.2.t: This is the king of sciences, the king of secrets, the supreme purifier, directly perceivable, righteous, joyful to practice, and imperishable.

9.5.t: And yet beings do not abide in Me. Behold My divine Yoga! My Self is the sustainer and originator of all beings, yet it does not dwell in them.

9.8.t: Presiding over My own nature, I send forth again and again this entire multitude of beings, who are helpless under the force of nature.

9.12.t: Their hopes are vain, their actions are vain, their knowledge is vain, and devoid of discernment, they take refuge in the deluding nature of fiends and demons.

9.15.t: And still others, worshipping through the sacrifice of knowledge, adore Me — as one, as distinct, and in manifold ways as the universal form facing everywhere.

9.16.t: I am the Vedic ritual, I am the sacrifice, I am the oblation to the ancestors, I am the medicinal herb, I am the mantra, I Myself am the clarified butter, I am the fire, and I am the act of offering.

9.17.t: I am the father of this universe, the mother, the sustainer, and the grandsire. I am the object of knowledge, the purifier, the sacred syllable Om, and also the Rig Veda, the Sama Veda, and the Yajur Veda.

9.18.t: I am the goal, the sustainer, the master, the witness, the abode, the refuge, and the friend. I am the origin, the dissolution, the foundation, the resting place, and the imperishable seed.

9.23.t: Even those devotees of other deities who worship them endowed with faith, they too worship Me alone, O son of Kunti, though not in the proper manner.

9.25.t: Those devoted to the gods go to the gods; those devoted to the ancestors go to the ancestors; those who worship the elemental beings go to the elemental beings; and those who worship Me come to Me.

9.28.t: Thus you shall be freed from the bondage of actions yielding good and bad results; with your mind steadfast in the yoga of renunciation, liberated, you shall come to Me.

9.31.t: He quickly becomes a righteous soul and attains everlasting peace. O son of Kunti, proclaim boldly that My devotee never perishes.

9.33.t: How much more then the holy Brahmanas and devoted royal sages! Having come to this impermanent and joyless world, worship Me.

9.34.t: Fix your mind on Me, be My devotee, worship Me, and bow down to Me. Thus disciplining yourself and taking Me as your supreme goal, you shall surely come to Me.

10.2.t: Neither the hosts of gods nor the great sages know My origin, for I am indeed the source of all the gods and the great sages in every way.

10.5.t: Nonviolence, equanimity, contentment, austerity, charity, fame, and infamy — these diverse dispositions of beings arise from Me alone.

10.6.t: The seven great sages, the four ancient ones, and likewise the Manus, endowed with My nature, were born from My mind — from them have come forth all these creatures in the world.

10.7.t: He who truly knows this glory and yogic power of Mine becomes established in unwavering yoga — there is no doubt about this.

10.8.t: I am the origin of all; from Me everything proceeds. Knowing this, the wise, endowed with deep devotion, worship Me.

10.9.t: With their minds fixed on Me and their lives surrendered to Me, enlightening one another and always speaking of Me, they find contentment and delight.

10.11.t: Out of compassion for them alone, I, dwelling within their hearts, destroy the darkness born of ignorance with the radiant lamp of knowledge.

10.14.t: I accept all this that You tell me as truth, O Keshava; for indeed, O Blessed Lord, neither the gods nor the demons know Your manifestation.

10.16.t: You alone can describe completely Your divine manifestations, by which manifestations You pervade and abide in all these worlds.

10.20.t: O Gudakesha, I am the Self seated in the hearts of all beings; I am the beginning, the middle, and also the end of all beings.

10.21.t: Among the Adityas I am Vishnu; among luminaries, the radiant sun; among the Maruts I am Marichi; and among the constellations I am the moon.

10.22.t: Among the Vedas I am the Sama Veda; among the gods I am Vasava. Among the senses I am the mind, and among living beings I am consciousness.

10.23.t: Among the Rudras I am Shankara, and among the Yakshas and Rakshasas I am the lord of wealth, Kubera. Among the Vasus I am Pavaka, the fire, and among the peaked mountains I am Meru.

10.27.t: Among horses, know Me to be Uchchaihshravas, born from the nectar; among lordly elephants, I am Airavata; and among men, I am the king.

10.28.t: Among weapons I am the thunderbolt; among cows I am Kamadhuk, the wish-fulfilling cow. I am Kandarpa, the god of love, among causes of procreation, and among serpents I am Vasuki.

10.29.t: Among the Nagas I am Ananta, among water-beings I am Varuna, among the ancestors I am Aryama, and among those who enforce order I am Yama.

10.30.t: Among the demons I am Prahlada, and among those that reckon I am time. Among animals I am the lion, and among birds I am Garuda.

10.33.t: Among letters I am the letter "A," and among compound words I am the Dvandva. I alone am inexhaustible Time, and I am the Creator facing in every direction.

10.35.t: Among the Sama hymns I am the Brihatsama; among meters I am the Gayatri. Of the months I am Margashirsha, and of the seasons I am the flower-bearing spring.

10.37.t: Among the Vrishnis I am Vasudeva, among the Pandavas I am Dhananjaya; among the sages I am Vyasa, and among the poets I am the poet Ushana.

11.3.t: O Supreme Lord, it is indeed so, as You have described Yourself. O Supreme Person, I wish to see Your divine form.

11.6.t: Behold the Adityas, the Vasus, the Rudras, the two Ashvins, and the Maruts as well. Behold many marvels never seen before, O Bharata.

11.9.t: Sanjaya said: Having spoken thus, O King, Hari, the great Lord of Yoga, then revealed to Partha His supreme divine form.

11.12.t: If the light of a thousand suns were to blaze forth all at once in the sky, that might be comparable to the radiance of that great Soul.

11.13.t: There, in the body of the God of gods, the Pandava then beheld the entire universe, divided in manifold ways, yet established as one.

11.15.t: Arjuna said: O God, I see in Your body all the gods and all the diverse hosts of beings, Lord Brahma seated on his lotus throne, Lord Shiva, all the sages, and the divine serpents.

11.18.t: You are the imperishable, the supreme One worthy of being known; You are the ultimate resting place of this universe. You are the undecaying protector of the eternal dharma; You are the everlasting Supreme Person—this is my conviction.

11.19.t: I see You without beginning, middle, or end, infinite in power, with endless arms, the sun and moon as Your eyes, Your mouth a blazing fire, scorching this entire universe with Your own radiance.

11.22.t: The Rudras, the Adityas, the Vasus, the Sadhyas, the Vishvadevas, the two Ashvins, the Maruts, and the ancestors, as well as the hosts of Gandharvas, Yakshas, Asuras, and Siddhas — all of them gaze upon You, struck with wonder.

11.30.t: You lick all around, devouring all the worlds on every side with Your blazing mouths. Filling the entire universe with Your radiance, Your fierce rays scorch all things, O Vishnu!

11.32.t: The Blessed Lord said: I am mighty Time, the destroyer of worlds, and I am here engaged in annihilating all people. Even without you, all the warriors arrayed in the opposing armies shall cease to exist.

11.33.t: Therefore, arise and win glory. Conquering your enemies, enjoy a prosperous kingdom. By Me alone have these warriors already been slain; be merely an instrument, O Savyasachin.

11.34.t: Drona and Bhishma and Jayadratha and Karna, as well as other brave warriors, have already been slain by Me; do you strike them down and do not be distressed — fight, and you shall conquer your enemies in battle.

11.37.t: And why should they not bow down to You, O Great Soul, who are greater even than Brahma, the original creator? O Infinite One, O Lord of the gods, O Abode of the universe, You are the imperishable — the being and the non-being, and that which is beyond both.

11.38.t: You are the primal God, the ancient Person; You are the supreme resting place of this universe. You are the knower and that which is to be known, and the supreme Abode. By You is this universe pervaded, O One of infinite forms!

11.39.t: You are Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the Moon, Prajapati, and the great-grandfather of all. Salutations, salutations to You a thousand times, and again and yet again, salutations, salutations to You!

11.40.t: Salutations to You from the front and from behind; salutations to You from all sides indeed, O All! You are of infinite power and immeasurable valor; You pervade everything, and therefore You are all.

11.42.t: And whatever disrespect was shown to You in jest — while at play, while resting, while sitting, or while eating, whether alone or in the presence of others, O Achyuta — for all that, I beg forgiveness of You, the immeasurable one.

11.44.t: Therefore, bowing down and prostrating my body, I implore Your grace, O adorable Lord. As a father forgives a son, as a friend forgives a friend, as a lover forgives the beloved, so should You forgive me, O God.

11.46.t: I wish to see You just as before — crowned, bearing a mace, with disc in hand. O thousand-armed one, O universal form, assume that very four-armed form again.

11.47.t: The Blessed Lord said: Being pleased with you, O Arjuna, this supreme form has been shown to you by Me through My own yogic power — resplendent, cosmic, infinite, and primeval, which no one other than you has ever seen before.

11.50.t: Sanjaya said: Having thus spoken to Arjuna, Vasudeva displayed His own form once again, and the great-souled one, assuming once more His gentle form, consoled the frightened Arjuna.

11.52.t: The Blessed Lord said: This form of Mine which you have seen is exceedingly difficult to behold; even the gods are ever longing to see this form.

11.54.t: But by single-minded devotion alone, O Arjuna, can I, in this form, be truly known, be seen, and be entered into, O scorcher of foes.

11.55.t: He who performs all actions for My sake, holds Me as the supreme goal, is devoted to Me, is free from attachment, and bears no enmity toward any being—he comes to Me, O son of Pandu.

12.1.t: Arjuna said: Those devotees who, ever steadfast, thus worship You, and those who worship the imperishable and unmanifest — of them, who are the most perfect in yoga?

12.5.t: Greater is the tribulation of those whose minds are attached to the Unmanifest; for the path of the Unmanifest is attained with great difficulty by the embodied.

12.12.t: Better indeed is knowledge than mere practice; meditation surpasses knowledge; renunciation of the fruits of actions excels meditation; and from such renunciation, peace follows immediately.

12.14.t: Ever content, steadily devoted in yoga, self-controlled, firm in conviction, with mind and intellect dedicated to Me — that devotee of Mine is dear to Me.

12.15.t: He from whom the world is not agitated, and who is not agitated by the world, who is free from joy, impatience, fear, and anxiety — he too is dear to Me.

12.17.t: He who neither rejoices nor hates, neither grieves nor desires, who renounces both good and evil, and who is full of devotion — he is dear to Me.

12.20.t: But those devotees who, endowed with faith and holding Me as the supreme goal, devoutly follow this immortal nectar of righteousness as declared — they are exceedingly dear to Me.

13.1.t: Arjuna said: O Keshava, I wish to know Prakriti and Purusha, the field and the knower of the field, knowledge and that which is to be known.

13.2.t: The Blessed Lord said: This body, O son of Kunti, is called the field; he who knows it is called the knower of the field by those who are knowers of that truth.

13.3.t: Know Me also as the knower of the field in all fields, O Bharata. The knowledge of the field and the knower of the field — that is true knowledge in My view.

13.5.t: This has been sung by the sages in manifold ways, separately in various Vedic hymns, and also through the words of the Brahma Sutras, which are full of reasoning and conclusive.

13.6.t: The five great elements, egoism, intellect, and the Unmanifest as well; the eleven senses, and the five objects of the senses;

13.7.t: Desire, aversion, happiness, sorrow, the aggregate, consciousness, and fortitude — this is the field, briefly described along with its modifications.

13.10.t: Non-attachment and absence of clinging to sons, spouse, home, and the like, and constant even-mindedness upon the occurrence of the desirable and the undesirable;

13.12.t: Constancy in knowledge of the Self, and contemplation directed toward the goal of knowledge of Reality — this is declared to be knowledge, and what is contrary to this is ignorance.

13.13.t: I shall declare that which is to be known, knowing which one attains immortality — the beginningless supreme Brahman, subordinate to Me, which is called neither being nor non-being.

13.14.t: It has hands and feet everywhere, eyes, heads, and mouths everywhere, ears everywhere in the world — it exists pervading all.

13.19.t: Thus the field, knowledge, and the knowable have been briefly described. My devotee, understanding this, becomes worthy of attaining My nature.

13.20.t: Know that both Prakriti and Purusha are beginningless; and know that all modifications and the gunas are born of Prakriti.

13.21.t: Nature is said to be the cause in the production of effects and their instruments, while the soul is said to be the cause in the experience of pleasure and pain.

13.22.t: The soul seated in Nature indeed experiences the qualities born of Nature; its attachment to the qualities is the cause of its birth in good and evil wombs.

13.27.t: Whatever being comes into existence, whether moving or unmoving, know that it arises from the union of the field and the knower of the field, O best of the Bharatas.

13.29.t: For one who sees the Lord equally present everywhere does not destroy the Self by the self, and thereby attains the supreme goal.

13.34.t: Just as the one sun illumines this entire world, so does the knower of the field illumine the entire field, O Bharata.

14.1.t: The Blessed Lord said: I shall again declare the supreme knowledge, the best among all knowledges, by knowing which all the sages have attained the highest perfection from here.

14.4.t: O son of Kunti, whatever forms come into being in all wombs, the great Prakrti is their womb, and I am the seed-giving father.

14.6.t: Among these, sattva, being stainless, is illuminating and free from affliction. O sinless one, it binds through attachment to happiness and through attachment to knowledge.

14.8.t: But know tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings; it binds them, O Bharata, through heedlessness, laziness, and sleep.

14.9.t: O Bharata, sattva binds one to happiness, rajas binds one to action, while tamas, veiling knowledge, binds one to heedlessness.

14.10.t: O Bharata, sattva prevails by overpowering rajas and tamas; rajas prevails by overpowering sattva and tamas; and likewise, tamas prevails by overpowering sattva and rajas.

14.12.t: Greed, activity, the undertaking of actions, restlessness, and craving — these arise when rajas predominates, O best of the Bharatas.

14.16.t: The fruit of righteous action, they say, is pure and sattvic; but the fruit of rajas is sorrow, and the fruit of tamas is ignorance.

14.17.t: From sattva arises knowledge, and from rajas, greed indeed. From tamas arise negligence and delusion, as well as ignorance.

14.18.t: Those established in sattva rise upward; those of rajas remain in the middle; and those abiding in the function of the lowest quality, the tamasic, go downward.

14.22.t: The Blessed Lord said: O Pandava, he neither hates illumination, activity, and delusion when they arise, nor longs for them when they cease.

14.25.t: He who is equal in honor and dishonor, equal toward the sides of friend and foe, and who has renounced all undertakings — he is said to have transcended the gunas.

15.1.t: The Blessed Lord said: They speak of the imperishable Ashvattha tree, with its roots above and branches below, whose leaves are the Vedic hymns; he who knows it is a knower of the Vedas.

15.2.t: Its branches spread downward and upward, nourished by the gunas, with sense-objects as their tender shoots; and below, in the world of humans, its secondary roots extend, giving rise to the bondage of action.

15.3.t: Its form is not perceived here as such, neither its end, nor its beginning, nor its foundation; having cut down this deep-rooted Ashvattha tree with the strong sword of detachment—

15.4.t: Then that state must be sought out, reaching which one does not return again; one should take refuge in that Primeval Person alone, from whom this ancient activity has streamed forth.

15.6.t: Neither the sun illumines that, nor the moon, nor fire. Having reached which, they do not return — that is My supreme abode.

15.7.t: An eternal fragment of Myself, having become the individual soul in the world of living beings, draws to itself the five senses with the mind as the sixth, all abiding in Nature.

15.8.t: When the lord of the body acquires a body and when he departs from it, he takes these along and goes, as the wind carries fragrances from their sources.

15.9.t: Presiding over the ear, the eye, the sense of touch, the tongue, and the nose, as well as the mind, this living soul savors the sense objects.

15.10.t: The deluded do not perceive it when it departs, when it stays, or when it experiences, accompanied by the qualities; but those who possess the eyes of knowledge behold it.

15.11.t: Striving yogis perceive this Self established within themselves, but those whose minds are unpurified and who lack discernment do not perceive it, even though they strive.

15.13.t: Entering the earth, I sustain all beings with My energy, and becoming the nourishing Soma, full of life-giving sap, I nourish all plants.

15.15.t: And I am seated in the hearts of all; from Me come memory, knowledge, and their loss. I alone am to be known through all the Vedas; I am the author of the Vedanta, and I alone am the knower of the Vedas.

15.16.t: There are these two Purushas in the world — the perishable and the imperishable. All beings are the perishable, and the unchanging one is called the imperishable.

15.17.t: But the Supreme Person is other than these, spoken of as the Supreme Self — He who, entering the three worlds, sustains them, the imperishable Lord.

15.18.t: Since I transcend the perishable and am higher even than the imperishable, I am celebrated in the world and in the Vedas as the Supreme Person.

15.19.t: He who, free from delusion, thus knows Me as the Supreme Person — he, knowing all, worships Me with his whole being, O Bharata.

16.2.t: Non-violence, truthfulness, absence of anger, renunciation, peacefulness, absence of slander, compassion toward all beings, freedom from covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and steadiness—

16.4.t: Hypocrisy, arrogance, conceit, anger, harshness, and ignorance — these belong to one who is born to the demoniac nature, O Partha.

16.6.t: In this world there are two types of created beings — the divine and the demoniac. The divine has been described at length; now hear from Me about the demoniac, O Partha.

16.8.t: They say that the world is without truth, without any foundation, without a God, born of nothing but mutual union — what else could there be? — with desire alone as its cause.

16.11.t: Beset by immeasurable anxieties that end only with death, regarding the gratification of desires as the highest aim, and convinced that this is all there is.

16.14.t: That enemy has been slain by me, and I shall slay others as well. I am the lord, I am the enjoyer, I am successful, I am powerful and happy.

16.15.t: I am wealthy, I am of noble birth — who else is equal to me? I shall perform sacrifices, I shall give charity, I shall rejoice" — thus they are deluded by ignorance.

16.16.t: Bewildered by countless anxious thoughts, enveloped in the net of delusion, and deeply attached to the enjoyment of sensual pleasures, they fall into a foul hell.

16.17.t: Self-conceited, stubborn, filled with the pride and intoxication of wealth, they perform sacrifices that are so in name only, with ostentation and without regard for scriptural injunctions.

16.18.t: Given over to egotism, force, arrogance, desire, and anger, these envious ones hate Me dwelling in their own and others' bodies.

16.19.t: Those hateful, cruel, and inauspicious beings—the lowest of men in the cycles of worldly existence—I hurl them again and again into demoniac wombs alone.

16.22.t: O son of Kunti, a person who is freed from these three gates to darkness strives for the welfare of the soul, and thereby attains the supreme goal.

16.24.t: Therefore, let the scripture be your authority in determining what is to be done and what is not to be done. Having understood what is declared by the injunctions of the scriptures, you should perform action here in this world.

17.2.t: The Blessed Lord said: The faith of embodied beings, born of their own nature, is threefold—sattvic, rajasic, and tamasic. Hear now about it.

17.4.t: Those of sattvic nature worship the gods; those of rajasic nature worship yakshas and rakshasas; and the others, persons of tamasic nature, worship the departed spirits and hosts of bhutas.

17.6.t: Those senseless ones who torment the aggregate of elements dwelling in the body, and also Me who dwell within the body — know them to be of demoniacal resolve.

17.12.t: But that sacrifice which is performed with an eye on the fruit and also for the sake of ostentation, know that sacrifice to be rajasic, O best of the Bharatas.

17.14.t: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, teachers, and the wise; cleanliness, straightforwardness, celibacy, and non-violence — these are called the austerity of the body.

17.17.t: That threefold austerity, practiced with supreme faith by steadfast persons who desire no fruit, is declared to be sattvic.

17.19.t: That austerity which is performed with a deluded resolve, through self-torture, or for the purpose of destroying another, is declared to be tamasic.

17.23.t: Om Tat Sat" — this is declared to be the threefold designation of Brahman. By that were the Brahmanas, the Vedas, and the sacrifices ordained of old.

17.27.t: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and charity is also called "Sat," and action performed for the sake of these is likewise designated as "Sat.

18.1.t: Arjuna said: I wish to know the truth of sannyasa, O mighty-armed one, and of tyaga separately, O Hrishikesha, O slayer of Keshi.

18.2.t: The Blessed Lord said: The learned understand sannyasa to be the giving up of desire-prompted actions, while the wise declare tyaga to be the relinquishment of the fruits of all actions.

18.4.t: Hear from Me the firm conclusion regarding tyaga, O best of the Bharatas; for tyaga, O tiger among men, has been declared to be of three kinds.

18.5.t: Acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity should not be abandoned but must certainly be performed, for sacrifice, charity, and austerity are indeed purifiers of the wise.

18.6.t: These actions too must certainly be performed, but with abandonment of attachment and desire for their fruits — this, O Partha, is my definite and supreme conviction.

18.7.t: The renunciation of prescribed duty is not justified; abandoning it out of delusion is declared to be tamasic.

18.10.t: The one who renounces, who is imbued with goodness, who is wise and whose doubts are cut away, neither hates disagreeable work nor clings to agreeable work.

18.14.t: The body as the seat of action, the doer, the various kinds of instruments, the many distinct efforts, and indeed destiny as the fifth among these.

18.19.t: Knowledge, action, and the doer are each declared to be of three kinds according to the distinction of the gunas, as stated in the science of the gunas. Hear of these also as they truly are.

18.24.t: But action that is performed by one desirous of fulfilling desires, or with egoism, and with much strain — that is declared to be rajasic.

18.25.t: That action which is undertaken out of delusion, without regard for consequences, loss, injury, and one's own ability, is declared to be tamasic.

18.26.t: The doer who is free from attachment, devoid of egoism, endowed with firmness and enthusiasm, and unaffected by success or failure, is said to be sattvic.

18.27.t: The doer who is passionate, who craves the fruits of action, who is greedy, violent by nature, impure, and subject to joy and sorrow, is declared to be rajasic.

18.29.t: Now hear the threefold division of intellect and also of firmness, according to the gunas, as it is being declared fully and distinctly, O Dhananjaya.

18.30.t: That intellect which knows action and renunciation, what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, what is to be feared and what is not to be feared, bondage and liberation — that intellect, O Partha, is sattvic.

18.31.t: That intellect by which one understands dharma and adharma, and what ought to be done and what ought not to be done, but understands them incorrectly — that intellect, O Partha, is rajasic.

18.33.t: That unwavering firmness by which one sustains the activities of the mind, the life-breath, and the senses through yoga — that firmness, O Partha, is sattvic.

18.34.t: But the firmness by which one holds fast to duty, pleasure, and wealth, O Arjuna, desiring their fruits out of attachment — that firmness, O Partha, is rajasic.

18.35.t: That firmness by which a foolish person does not relinquish sleep, fear, grief, despair, and also conceit — that resolve, O Partha, is tamasic.

18.36.t: Now hear from Me, O best of the Bharatas, about the threefold nature of happiness — that in which one rejoices through practice and comes to the end of sorrow.

18.37.t: That happiness which is like poison in the beginning but like nectar in the end, born from the serenity of one's own intellect focused on the Self — that is declared to be sattvic.

18.42.t: Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, patience, uprightness, knowledge, wisdom, and faith in God — these are the duties of a Brahmana, born of his own nature.

18.43.t: Valor, splendor, fortitude, dexterity, and also not fleeing from battle, generosity, and lordliness — these are the duties of the Kshatriyas, born of their own nature.

18.49.t: He whose intellect is unattached everywhere, who has conquered his self, and from whom desire has departed, attains through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action.

18.50.t: Learn from Me in brief, O son of Kunti, how one who has attained perfection also reaches Brahman, which is the supreme consummation of knowledge.

18.51.t: Endowed with a purified intellect, restraining oneself with firmness, relinquishing the objects of the senses beginning with sound, and casting aside attachment and hatred;

18.52.t: Resorting to solitude, eating lightly, with speech, body, and mind restrained, ever devoted to the yoga of meditation, and having taken refuge in dispassion—

18.53.t: Having abandoned egotism, force, arrogance, desire, anger, and possessiveness, free from the sense of "mine" and peaceful, one is fit for becoming Brahman.

18.55.t: Through devotion he comes to know Me in truth — how great I am and who I am. Then, having known Me in truth, he enters into Me immediately thereafter.

18.56.t: Even while always performing all actions, one who takes full refuge in Me attains, by My grace, the eternal and imperishable state.

18.57.t: Mentally renouncing all actions to Me, having Me as the supreme goal, taking shelter in the yoga of intellect, fix your mind on Me always.

18.64.t: Listen again to My supreme word, the most secret of all; you are very dear to Me, and therefore I shall speak what is for your benefit.

18.66.t: Abandoning all dharmas, take refuge in Me alone. I shall liberate you from all sins; do not grieve.

18.67.t: This should never be spoken by you to one who lacks austerity, nor to one who is without devotion, nor to one who does not wish to listen, nor to one who speaks ill of Me.

18.71.t: And the person who listens to this with faith and without malice, he too, liberated, shall attain the auspicious worlds of those of virtuous deeds.

18.74.t: Sanjaya said: Thus I have heard this wonderful conversation between Vasudeva and the great-souled Partha, which causes the hair to stand on end.

18.77.t: And remembering again and again that most wondrous form of Hari, great is my astonishment, O King, and I rejoice again and again.

18.78.t: Wherever there is Krishna, the Lord of Yoga, and wherever is Partha, the wielder of the bow, there are fortune, victory, prosperity, and steadfast righteousness — this is my conviction.
